verdict.rationale: Granola documents API key creation in which the creator picks which note access scopes the key includes, so scoped credentials for an agent are a first-party feature. Admins can also create workspace keys, but these don't expire, and API keys require a Business or Enterprise plan. Only one line describes the scopes, so how fine-grained least-privilege can be (e.g., read-only vs. write, per-folder) is unproven. Missing for 10: documented scope list and granularity, key expiry/rotation controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: When you create an API key, you choose which note access scopes it should include.
Workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can also create workspace API keys. These belong to the workspace rather than an individual user, don't expire
